generated.title: Can a Magnitude 10 Earthquake Actually Happen? #shorts
generated.description:
We've seen magnitude 9.5. But could Earth ever produce a 10?

The largest earthquake ever recorded was magnitude 9.5 in Chile in 1960, on a fault about 1,000 kilometers long. Bigger earthquakes need longer faults, so a magnitude 10 would need a much longer one. According to the USGS, no fault that long is known to exist, so scientists don't expect a magnitude 10.

The fault-length bars in this video are schematic illustrations, not data or footage. Tomorrow: Chile 1960, the earthquake that set the record.

Part of the Earthquake Science Explained series. Subscribe to Next Huge Quake for more earthquake science.
